description: Making sure every astronaut is healthy when they fly to the space!
summary:
Imagining astronauts suffering from short-term and long-term health issues silently without them knowing it. They do not have a system to track their health statuses and know what to do. Not only that, they also cannot manage their health properly, such as meals, sleep, workouts, and so on.'

Aegis is here to help and motivate them to do so. Aegis detects health metrics from astronauts when they are on a mission, helping astronauts to track, monitor, improve, and alert their health statuses comprehensively. Aegis also works like an ordinary health watch that tracks their calorie intake, sleep status, workout status, and so on.

I believed that astronauts deserve great health when they are on missions, and that motivates me to do so.
details:
How Does It Work?

Aegis is a connected system made of two parts: Aegis Watch and Aegis Board.

Aegis Watch (The Astronaut’s Personal Helper): A smartwatch that checks important health signs and daily habits, such as sleep quality, food calories, heart rate, and blood pressure. When it notices a problem, it sends quick warnings and easy steps to help the astronaut recover. To keep astronauts excited about their health, it uses simple games and daily goals to make exercise, drinking water, and eating well feel rewarding.

Aegis Board (The Headquarters Dashboard): A main screen for space doctors and mission leaders on Earth. It collects live health data from the crew and safety data from the spaceship. It shows health changes over time, warns leaders early if an astronaut is at risk, and gives helpful advice based on those patterns.

Benefits?

Early Warnings Before Emergencies: Notices small drops in health or sleep quality early, stopping small problems from becoming serious emergencies.

Clear, Personal Advice: Turns difficult medical numbers into easy, step-by-step tips made for each astronaut's body.

Strong Daily Motivation: Uses fun goals and progress tracking to help astronauts stay active and eat well every day.

Better Team Planning: Gives mission leaders a quick, clear view of how healthy and ready the whole crew is in one place.

Impact?

Safer Long Space Trips: Protects astronauts from space health problems like weak muscles, extreme tiredness, and heart stress.

Less Crew Stress: Helps astronauts stay mentally and physically strong during difficult, lonely trips far from Earth.

Smart Independent Health Care: Helps crews handle medical problems on their own when they cannot get quick help from Earth.

Helpful Technology for Earth: Creates offline health tools that can also help remote clinics, disaster areas, and country villages on Earth.

Tools & Tech?

App Design: React with TypeScript (to build a fast, reliable, and easy-to-use screen for both the watch and the dashboard)

Smart AI Tools: Google AI Studio and AI APIs (to check health data, give personal recovery tips, and predict dangers)

What do Aegis consider?

No Internet or Signal Delays: Deep-space trips can have signal delays of over 20 minutes or lose connection completely. Aegis can check health data and give smart medical advice on its own without needing a connection to Earth.

Live Space Dangers: Connects to spaceship sensors to watch for dangerous radiation, too much carbon dioxide, low oxygen, and temperature changes, warning astronauts the second their environment becomes unsafe.

Zero Gravity and Sleep Changes: Understands that space has no normal day-and-night cycle and zero gravity changes how fluids move in the body. It adjusts sleep times, water goals, and exercise plans to match.

Heavy Work and Loneliness: Looks at how hard the crew is working and how long they have been alone, helping tell the difference between normal physical tiredness and mental stress.
